The omakase runs to small dishes and about a dozen nigiri, with standouts like abalone steamed for six hours in its liver sauce (mixed with a little sushi rice at the end), sweet uni, medium-fatty tuna and anago with a rich sauce. The pairing pours a glass every two or three courses from a list of over 200 champagnes, with a featured house each month, and staff guide non-experts well. Dinner only, all guests start together; reserve for an anniversary night. One diner found a grilled fish watery.

osaka_furatto_curry_ya_inari.notes: [Curry · a ¥980 chicken katsu curry behind JR Namba, Inari] A small, warm curry shop on a quiet street about ten minutes from JR Namba that stays open through the afternoon. The order is the chicken katsu curry (¥980): the katsu is the surprise, crisp outside and tender and juicy within, over a mild, homestyle European curry sweet with onion. Natto ajillo and a shungiku salad are unusual extras. Friendly staff; courses with two hours of drinks are ¥5,500. One diner found a group course thin and one had a Tabelog booking go unseen. Smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_kinoko_no_sato_minamisenba.notes: [Mushroom · creative mushroom courses, Minami-Senba] A small, pleasant restaurant near Shinsaibashi where nearly everything at dinner is mushrooms. Staff explain the mushrooms and how to eat each dish. Seasoning is gentle and the umami is deep. Try the mushroom sake or gin. Weekday lunch is a different menu: soup curry only. Reserve for dinner. One diner got soggy tempura.

osaka_curry_ya_dekkao_minamisenba.notes: [Curry · Sri Lankan-style curry plates, Minami-Senba] A busy, homey second-floor curry shop near Shinsaibashi, easy to miss from the street, serving Sri Lankan-style curry adapted to Japanese tastes: spicy but approachable. Build a plate around the bone-in chicken curry and one or two of the four or five daily curries, such as clam and tomato or spicy coconut tuna; the Dekkao Special is ¥1,300 and the Greedy version adds a second curry and more sides for ¥1,650. Taste each curry and side first, then mix it all together. Warm, smiling staff. Expect a line at opening. Mostly lunch; dinner Tuesdays and Thursdays. Closed Sundays. PayPay, no cards.

chef_bio.philosophy: Sri Lankan curry blended with Japanese cooking to suit Japanese tastes (September 2026 review, citing the owner).

Birthday plates on request; friendly staff. It fills up, so reserve. Closed Mondays.

osaka_goyakura_minamisenba.notes: [Curry · a one-person dashi curry shop, Minami-Senba] A calm, lunch-only curry counter behind a heavy door in Minami-Senba, where the owner cooks alone and calls the style "Ware": thick curries built on Japanese dashi, aromatic rather than hot. Four pickles sit on the side. House rule: wait for your order to be taken. Cash only; smoking allowed. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

osaka_shinmachi_curry.notes: [Curry · dashi-based spice curry, Shinmachi] A small curry counter under a green awning in Shinmachi, run by two people whose bright, attentive service, remembering returning faces, is half the appeal. The curry is light and soupy, built on dashi rather than heat: choose a chicken-broth base with Shodoshima soy sauce or a katsuobushi dashi with soy milk, then chicken-and-pork or fish keema, and mix in the sides, such as a crunchy gizzard achar. Add the ¥200 squid and clam Thai curry if it's on. Shrimp curry Thursdays to Saturdays. Open through 4 pm, handy for a late lunch. Cash only. Closed Sundays.

osaka_savatomy_azuchimachi.notes: [Chinese · a creative Chinese bar of small plates, Azuchimachi] A stylish, busy Chinese bar near Sakaisuji-Honmachi where colorful small plates are sized for two to share. The must-order is the seared bonito in the house red sauce, smoky and gently spicy; add the moist drool chicken, fluffy anago, dim sum and, in season, oyster spring rolls, with an 18-year Shaoxing wine, straight or with soda. Seasoning is balanced enough for friends who avoid heat. Lunch is a bargain, with dan dan noodles, mapo tofu or a fuller set for about ¥2,000; one weekday it was full soon after 11:30. Reserve for dinner. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Creative Chinese restaurant and bar (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The first bite of the seared bonito was shocking. It was unlike any seared bonito I had ever tasted before. The smoky aroma and slightly spicy flavor were incredible." — October 2026, lunch.
"Each dish was perfectly portioned for sharing between two people, allowing us to enjoy a variety of menu items in small bites." — October 2026.

osaka_men_chu_minamihorie.notes: [Ramen · an old-style chicken shoyu shop, Minami-Horie] A quiet neighborhood ramen shop in western Minami-Horie with warm, attentive staff. The bowls are light and old-fashioned: a chicken shoyu broth that tastes mild at first and deepens as the tare at the bottom mixes in, medium-thin straight noodles, and tender, well-marinated chashu and good menma, which even diners who found the soup lacking praise. The Horie Ramen (¥930) is the house bowl, and a small fried rice (¥420) makes a cheap set. Reviews are split on the broth, so come for something gentle. Open late; closed Mondays. Cash only.

anecdotes.text: "At first sip, the broth seemed a bit light, but as I continued eating, the flavor intensified. This was likely due to the tare that had settled at the bottom of the bowl mixing in." — July 2026, chicken shoyu ramen ¥770.
"The chashu was tender and well-marinated, making it delicious." — September 2026, Horie Ramen.

No cards; QR accepted (Tabelog). Ashtrays on the counter and tables; smoking allowed (April 2026).
osaka_ganbare_hourai_minamihorie.notes: [Ramen · a cozy chicken-paitan ramen and Chinese-food spot, Minami-Horie] A café-like ramen and Chinese-food shop facing Takadaibashi Park; one diner has ordered takeout from it for years. The chicken paitan comes in shio or shoyu, rich but not heavy, with a seasoned egg included at no charge, thick melt-in-the-mouth chashu, chopped onion and fried garlic. Pair a half bowl (¥800) with the fluffy small fried rice (¥350) for a cheap loop of rice, soup and chashu. There are also dan dan noodles, Taiwanese mazesoba, gyoza and a long drinks list. Smoking allowed. Hours vary; check before going.

anecdotes.text: "The creamy richness of the paitan broth perfectly complements the savory aroma of the soy sauce. It's rich yet not too heavy…" — June 2026, half Shoyu Paitan Ramen ¥800.
"What's interesting is that this place includes a flavored egg as a default, rather than as a paid option." — January 2026, salt chicken paitan ramen.

osaka_shuki_lanzhou_namba.notes: [Lanzhou noodles · hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles and lamb skewers, Namba-naka] A big, no-frills Chinese noodle house between Namba and Daikokucho. The draw is hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles in a light, spiced beef-bone broth finished with chili oil and cilantro, with your pick of eight noodle widths, chewy almost like udon at the wide end; Set A (¥1,200) adds small side dishes. Add cumin-spiced lamb skewers, or try the sour-and-spicy vermicelli and a cheap lamb-with-cumin set. Splash in the table vinegar halfway. Open every day. Ask for the non-smoking section.
